source.prompt: Two-stage generation via Cloudflare AI Gateway (unified billing, gateway kaede-assets — the walk-quality bench of ROADMAP Phase 5 ①b(c), 2026-08-08). Stage 1 input: the character's stand frame on a 720x720 pure #00FF00 canvas (character ~470px tall, feet on y=640; derived from the previous sheet's stand cell, itself generated from reference.png). Stage 2, model alibaba/wan-2.7-i2v (image-to-video), prompt: 'The chibi boy game character from the image walks in place, treadmill-style, without moving across the frame. An exaggerated cartoon game walk cycle like classic 2D side-scrolling games: BIG strides with legs swinging far forward and far back, knees lifting high on each step, and arms swinging WIDELY — the near arm swings clearly in front of his chest, then far behind his back, opposite to the legs. Legs strictly alternate: right leg steps forward, then left leg steps forward. He keeps facing right in 3/4 view. The camera is completely static, no zoom, no pan. The flat pure green #00FF00 chroma-key background stays perfectly unchanged and empty. The character stays centered with his feet returning to the same ground line every step. Constant even lighting, no shadows.' Output: 5s 30fps 1440x1440 video. The committed sheet is video frames n0 (stand = the input image as rendered), n66 (walk-a: contact, near arm swung back), n72 (walk-b: passing), n78 (walk-c: the opposite contact, near arm swung front), n84 (walk-d: the opposite passing), each cropped to the center 760px, downscaled 2x into one row, with shadowed-green background pixels flattened to solid green (the video adds a soft ground shadow despite the prompt). Why a video model: static image models cannot produce the alternating contact poses — text-grid, mirror-instruction and reference-edit attempts all collapse both contacts onto one stride (measured on the previous sheet and re-confirmed on seedream-4.5 / nano-banana-2 in this bench), and a nano-banana-2 restyle pass over the video frames drifted the poses back to one stride too. A video model renders true leg alternation because motion consistency is what it is trained on; the exaggerated-swing prompt is what makes the alternation readable at 96px (arm clearly front vs clearly back). Post-composition: the stand frame's head (everything above its detected neck pinch, +14px chin overlap) is composited onto every walk frame at that frame's own neck anchor, replacing the video-rendered head — the video model repaints the face/hair every frame and the resulting outline wobble read as mud/morphing at game scale (2026-08-08 review); a pixel-identical head with per-frame neck placement keeps the natural head bob while eliminating the wobble. This composite also doubles as the first validation of the ①d head-group separation spec (head as a layer anchored at neck).
